title.zh: 卷329 列傳一百十六 宋元俊 薛琮 张芝元 董天弼 柴大纪
title.en: Volume 329 Biographies 116: Song Yuanjun, Xue Cong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Dong Tianbi, Chai Daji
title.raw: 卷329 列傳一百十六 宋元俊 薛琮 张芝元 董天弼 柴大纪

sentences.zh: 列傳一百十六

translations.literal: Biographies 116
translations.idiomatic: Biography 116

sentences.zh: 宋元俊薛琮張芝元董天弼柴大紀

translations.literal: Song Yuanjun, Xue Cong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Dong Tianbi, Chai Daji
translations.idiomatic: Song Yuanjun, Xue Cong, Zhang Zhiyuan, Dong Tianbi, and Chai Daji

sentences.zh: 宋元俊，字甸芳，江南懷遠人。

translations.literal: Song Yuanjun, whose style name was Dianfang, was a man of Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yuanjun, courtesy name Dianfang, came from Huaiyuan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 以武進士授四川成都營守備，遷懷遠營都司。

translations.literal: By military jinshi degree he was appointed garrison commandant of the Chengdu Camp in Sichuan, and was transferred to brigade commander of the Huaiyuan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military examinations, he was appointed garrison commandant of the Chengdu Camp in Sichuan and later promoted to brigade commander of the Huaiyuan Camp.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十年，孔撒、麻書兩土司構釁，金川、綽斯甲布兩土司乘隙為亂，元俊為撫定，集孔撒、麻書、金川、綽斯甲布、革布什咱、綽沃、白立、章谷、瞻對諸土司斷曲直，使頂經立誓。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Qianlong, the two native chieftains of Kongsa and Mashu provoked trouble; the chieftains of Jinchuan and Chosichab took advantage of the opening to rebel. Yuanjun was sent to pacify and settle matters. He gathered the chieftains of Kongsa, Mashu, Jinchuan, Chosichab, Geshizhai, Zhuowo, Baili, Zhanggu, and Zhando, judged right and wrong, and had them swear oaths upon scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 20 (1755), the Kongsa and Mashu chieftains stirred up trouble, and the Jinchuan and Chosichab chieftains seized the moment to rise in revolt. Yuanjun was appointed to pacify the region. He convened the chieftains of Kongsa, Mashu, Jinchuan, Chosichab, Geshizhai, Zhuowo, Baili, Zhanggu, Zhando, and others, adjudicated their disputes, and had them swear binding oaths on scripture.

sentences.zh: 累遷阜和營游擊。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting colonel of the Fuhe Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to acting colonel of the Fuhe Camp.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，金川土司郎卡侵丹壩、綽斯甲布兩土司，諸土司請兵，署總督阿桂、提督岳鍾琪奏令元俊偕署副將長清諭各土司合兵進剿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Jinchuan chieftain Langka invaded the two chieftains of Dandan and Chosichab; the various chieftains requested troops. Acting Governor Agui and Provincial Military Commissioner Yue Zhongqi memorialized ordering Yuanjun together with Acting Deputy General Chang Qing to instruct the various chieftains to combine forces and advance in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29 (1764), the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Dandan and Chosichab chieftains, and the affected chieftains appealed for military aid. Acting Governor Agui and Provincial Military Commissioner Yue Zhongqi recommended that Yuanjun, together with Acting Deputy General Chang Qing, urge the chieftains to unite their forces for a joint punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 移漳臘營參將，坐事左遷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to battalion major of the Zhangla Camp, and was demoted for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as battalion major of the Zhangla Camp but was later demoted after being implicated in a disciplinary matter.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，小金川土司澤旺之子僧格桑掠鄂克什，阿桂檄元俊宣諭僧格桑還侵地及所掠番民。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Senggesang, son of the Little Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, raided Ekezhi. Agui issued an order to Yuanjun to proclaim and instruct Senggesang to return the invaded territory and the tribal people he had seized.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 35 (1770), Senggesang, son of the Little Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, raided Ekezhi. Agui directed Yuanjun to demand that Senggesang restore the seized lands and return the tribal subjects he had carried off.

sentences.zh: 复補阜和營游擊。

translations.literal: He was again restored to acting colonel of the Fuhe Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently reinstated as acting colonel of the Fuhe Camp.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，革布什咱頭人結郎卡子索諾木據革布什咱官寨，戕土司策楞多布丹，總督阿爾泰復令元俊往宣諭。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, the Geshizhai headman Jielangka's son Sonam occupied the Geshizhai official stockade and killed the chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor Altai again ordered Yuanjun to go and proclaim instructions.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 (1771), Sonam, son of the Geshizhai headman Jielangka, seized the Geshizhai official fortress and murdered Chieftain Celeng Duobudan. Governor Altai once again dispatched Yuanjun to deliver an imperial admonition.

sentences.zh: 小金川圍鄂克什、達木巴宗，侵明正土司，據納頂寨，元俊與參將薛琮、都司李天佑率兵討之，收納頂寨，進攻索布大寨。

translations.literal: Little Jinchuan besieged Ekezhi and Damubazong, invaded the Mingzheng chieftain, and held Nadai Stockade. Yuanjun together with Battalion Major Xue Cong and Brigade Commander Li Tianyou led troops to attack them, recovered Nadai Stockade, and advanced to attack the great stockade of Suobu.
translations.idiomatic: Little Jinchuan forces besieged Ekezhi and Damubazong, encroached on the Mingzheng chieftain's domain, and occupied Nadai Stockade. Yuanjun, Battalion Major Xue Cong, and Brigade Commander Li Tianyou led a punitive force that retook Nadai and pressed the attack on Suobu's main fortress.

sentences.zh: 琮率兵自山梁潛度，元俊與天佑渡河夾擊，獲石卡十八，屢戰皆捷，明正土司碉寨七百餘盡复。

translations.literal: Cong led troops in a secret crossing over the mountain ridge; Yuanjun and Tianyou crossed the river in a pincer attack, capturing eighteen stone forts. Battle after battle was victorious, and more than seven hundred towers and stockades of the Mingzheng chieftain were all recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cong led his men in a stealthy crossing along the mountain ridge while Yuanjun and Li Tianyou forded the river for a converging assault. They captured eighteen stone forts and won victory after victory until more than seven hundred Mingzheng towers and stockades had been fully restored.

sentences.zh: 師入小金川境，取噶中拉、莫如納、扎功拉等地，進克納咱。

translations.literal: The army entered Little Jinchuan territory, took Gazhongla, Moruna, Zhagongla, and other places, and advanced to capture Nazan.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed into Little Jinchuan territory, seized Gazhongla, Moruna, Zhagongla, and neighboring positions, and went on to capture Nazan.

sentences.zh: 阿爾泰及侍郎桂林以聞，擢松潘鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Altai and Vice Minister Guilin reported this to the throne, and Yuanjun was promoted to brigade general of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: Altai and Vice Minister Guilin reported his achievements to the throne, and Yuanjun was promoted to brigade general commanding the Songpan garrison.

sentences.zh: 師攻甲木，賊據喇嘛寺為固。

translations.literal: The army attacked Jiamu; the rebels held the Lama Temple as a strong point.
translations.idiomatic: When the army assaulted Jiamu, the rebels fortified themselves in the Lama Temple.

sentences.zh: 元俊及守備陳定國攻破之，盡收所屬城、卡、碉、寨，據墨爾多山梁。

translations.literal: Yuanjun and Garrison Commandant Chen Dingguo stormed and broke it, recovering all subordinate towns, passes, towers, and stockades, and holding the Mo'erduo mountain ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun and Garrison Commandant Chen Dingguo stormed the temple and broke the rebel line, recovering every affiliated town, pass, tower, and stockade before securing the Mo'erduo ridge.

sentences.zh: 師復進，天佑、定國攻西山梁，元俊同侍衛六十一、參將巴克坦布等自喇嘛寺繞攻郭松，參領普寧自西山麓沿河攻甲木，侍衛哈青阿及琮自東山麓攻卡丫。

translations.literal: The army advanced again: Tianyou and Dingguo attacked the western mountain ridge; Yuanjun together with Bodyguard Liushiyi, Battalion Major Baketanbu, and others made a flanking attack on Guosong from around the Lama Temple; Company Commander Puning attacked Jiamu along the river from the western foothills; Bodyguard Haqing'a and Cong attacked Kaya from the eastern foothills.
translations.idiomatic: The army pressed forward again on several axes: Li Tianyou and Chen Dingguo struck the western ridge; Yuanjun, Bodyguard Liushiyi, Battalion Major Baketanbu, and others swung around the Lama Temple to assault Guosong; Company Commander Puning moved up the river from the western foothills against Jiamu; and Bodyguard Haqing'a and Xue Cong attacked Kaya from the east.

sentences.zh: 師行以夜半，戰自卯至巳，卡丫、郭松、甲木皆克。

translations.literal: The army marched at midnight; fighting lasted from the hour mao to the hour si; Kaya, Guosong, and Jiamu were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: The columns moved out at midnight and fought from dawn until mid-morning; Kaya, Guosong, and Jiamu all fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 賜元俊孔雀翎。

translations.literal: Yuanjun was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun was awarded the peacock feather insignia of distinction.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，師攻革布​​什咱，元俊請於桂林，分兵為五道：一自郭宗濟野宗攻木巴拉博租；

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, as the army attacked Geshizhai, Yuanjun requested of Guilin to divide the forces into five routes: one from Guozong Jiyezong to attack Mubalabozu;
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37 (1772), during the campaign against Geshizhai, Yuanjun proposed to Guilin a five-pronged advance: the first column would move from Guozong Jiyezong against Mubalabozu;

sentences.zh: 一自章谷渡河夾攻，俾賊前後受敵，兩軍既合，先據默資溝，截金川來路，進取吉地官寨；

translations.literal: one to cross the river from Zhanggu in a pincer attack so that the rebels would be attacked front and rear; once the two armies had joined, first to seize Mozi Gorge, cut off Jinchuan's route of advance, and proceed to take the Jidi official stockade;
translations.idiomatic: a second would cross from Zhanggu to hit the enemy from both front and rear; once the two columns united, they would first secure Mozi Gorge, sever Jinchuan's line of reinforcement, and then advance on the Jidi official fortress;

sentences.zh: 一自巴旺之高石、嘉舉諸山，分道攻薩瑪多監藏布覺，取吉地；

translations.literal: one from the Gaoshi, Jiaju, and other mountains of Bawang, dividing forces to attack Samaduo Jianzang Bujue and take Jidi;
translations.idiomatic: a third would strike from the Gaoshi and Jiaju heights of Bawang in separate detachments against Samaduo Jianzang Bujue and seize Jidi;

sentences.zh: 一自茂紐攻沙沖；

translations.literal: one from Maoniu to attack Shachong;
translations.idiomatic: a fourth would advance from Maoniu against Shachong;

sentences.zh: 一自喀勒塔爾攻黨哩，會兵取丹東。

translations.literal: one from Kaleta'er to attack Dangli, converging forces to take Dandong.
translations.idiomatic: and a fifth would move from Kaleta'er against Dangli before converging to capture Dandong.

sentences.zh: 策定，元俊及游擊吳錦江等自章谷渡河據格藏橋，哈青阿、天佑出郭宗濟野宗，兩隊軍夾攻，賊驚潰，遂克木巴拉博租、薩瑪多監藏布覺諸地。

translations.literal: Once the plan was settled, Yuanjun and Acting Colonel Wu Jinjiang and others crossed the river from Zhanggu and held Gezang Bridge; Haqing'a and Tianyou came out from Guozong Jiyezong; the two columns attacked in concert, the rebels were startled and routed, and Mubalabozu, Samaduo Jianzang Bujue, and other places were then captured.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was adopted. Yuanjun and Acting Colonel Wu Jinjiang crossed from Zhanggu and seized Gezang Bridge, while Haqing'a and Li Tianyou advanced from Guozong Jiyezong. The converging columns routed the stunned rebels and took Mubalabozu, Samaduo Jianzang Bujue, and neighboring strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 進克吉地官寨及默資溝。

translations.literal: They advanced and captured the Jidi official stockade and Mozi Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: The army then pressed forward and captured the Jidi official fortress together with Mozi Gorge.

sentences.zh: 參將常泰等克黨哩，都司李天貴等克沙沖，元俊复克丹東。

translations.literal: Battalion Major Chang Tai and others captured Dangli; Brigade Commander Li Tiangui and others captured Shachong; Yuanjun again captured Dandong.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion Major Chang Tai took Dangli, Brigade Commander Li Tiangui seized Shachong, and Yuanjun recovered Dandong as well.

sentences.zh: 复革布什咱地三百餘裡，民戶二千餘。

translations.literal: More than three hundred li of Geshizhai territory was recovered, with more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred li of Geshizhai territory was restored, along with more than two thousand subject households.

sentences.zh: 桂林遣陳定國調綽斯甲布兵駐軍界上，備調遣。

translations.literal: Guilin sent Chen Dingguo to mobilize Chosichab troops and station them on the border, ready for deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin ordered Chen Dingguo to muster Chosichab troops and hold them along the frontier for possible deployment.

sentences.zh: 上責桂林不令元俊乘勝取金川。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Guilin for not letting Yuanjun press the victory to take Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Guilin for failing to let Yuanjun exploit the victory and press on into Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 元俊旋與散秩大臣阿爾泰劾桂林欺誑及諸罪狀，上為奪桂林職，令阿爾泰署四川總督，命額駙、尚書、公福隆安按治。

translations.literal: Yuanjun then together with Minister without Portfolio Altai impeached Guilin for deception and various offenses; the emperor thereupon stripped Guilin of his post, ordered Altai to act as Governor of Sichuan, and commanded Imperial Son-in-law, Minister, and Duke Fu Long'an to investigate and settle the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun soon joined Minister without Portfolio Altai in impeaching Guilin for deception and related offenses. The emperor removed Guilin from office, appointed Altai acting Governor of Sichuan, and dispatched Imperial Son-in-law, Minister, and Duke Fu Long'an to conduct a formal investigation.

sentences.zh: 未至，詔元俊督兵赴綽斯甲布率土兵進攻金川。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, an edict ordered Yuanjun to supervise troops and proceed to Chosichab to lead native soldiers in an attack on Jinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before Fu Long'an arrived, an edict directed Yuanjun to take command at Chosichab and lead native levies in an assault on Jinchuan.

sentences.zh: 元俊奏：「自戰失利，士氣消沮，現在兵力不足並按兩金川。

translations.literal: Yuanjun memorialized: "Since the defeat in battle, morale has flagged; at present the troops are insufficient to press both Jinchuans at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun memorialized: "Since our recent defeats morale has collapsed, and the forces now on hand are not enough to tackle both Jinchuans simultaneously.

sentences.zh: 請敕調湖南、湖北、山西、甘肅兵二萬，分三道進軍，計兩月可竟事。

translations.literal: I request an imperial order to transfer twenty thousand troops from Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, and Gansu, advancing in three columns; it is estimated the affair can be concluded within two months."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order twenty thousand reinforcements from Hunan, Hubei, Shanxi, and Gansu to advance in three columns; the campaign could then be finished within two months."

sentences.zh: 」上以元俊請益師，未免張皇，令福隆安會阿爾泰、阿桂與元俊詳悉覈計。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Yuanjun's request for additional troops somewhat alarmist, ordered Fu Long'an to meet with Altai, Agui, and Yuanjun for a thorough review and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded Yuanjun's call for reinforcements as unduly alarmist and ordered Fu Long'an to confer with Altai, Agui, and Yuanjun for a detailed reassessment of the plan.

sentences.zh: 上諭軍機大臣，謂：「元俊能治事，熟番情；

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the Grand Council, saying: "Yuanjun can handle affairs and is thoroughly familiar with tribal conditions;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the Grand Council: "Yuanjun is capable and thoroughly understands frontier tribal affairs;

sentences.zh: 但其人似狡猾好事，當留意駕馭。

translations.literal: but this man seems crafty and fond of meddling; care should be taken in managing him."
translations.idiomatic: but he also seems crafty and prone to stirring trouble, so he must be kept firmly in hand."

sentences.zh: 尋，福隆安疏陳所劾桂林狀不實，上以方進兵，元俊熟番情，諸事不必窮究；

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Fu Long'an memorialized that the charges against Guilin were not substantiated. The emperor, since troops were then advancing, and Yuanjun was thoroughly familiar with tribal conditions, said that these matters need not be pursued to the end;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fu Long'an reported that the charges against Guilin could not be substantiated. With the campaign still under way and Yuanjun indispensable for tribal affairs, the emperor declared that the matter need not be pursued further;

sentences.zh: 惟言：「桂林以白金畀金川贖被掠官兵罪最重，今汪承霈自承出其意。

translations.literal: only saying: "Guilin's crime of giving white silver to Jinchuan to ransom captured officers and soldiers is the most serious; now Wang Chengpei has confessed that the idea came from him.
translations.idiomatic: except to note: "Guilin's gravest offense was paying Jinchuan silver to ransom captured officers and men; Wang Chengpei has now confessed that the scheme originated with him.

sentences.zh: 承霈以曹司從軍，不當與其事。

translations.literal: Chengpei, as a clerical officer following the army, ought not to have been involved in such affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As a clerical officer attached to the campaign, Chengpei should never have been involved in such dealings.

sentences.zh: 當詰汪騰龍，成信讞。

translations.literal: Wang Tenglong should be interrogated so that a credible verdict may be reached."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tenglong must be interrogated until the truth is established."

sentences.zh: 」福隆安复疏言：「騰龍以金囑王萬邦待巴旺、布拉底克歸迷道官兵予金為賞，元俊誘萬邦令具札言桂林使贖被掠官兵。

translations.literal: " Fu Long'an again memorialized, saying: "Tenglong entrusted gold to Wang Wanbang to wait until the officers and soldiers of Bawang and Buladike who had lost their way returned, and then give gold as a reward. Yuanjun induced Wanbang to draw up a letter stating that Guilin had sent ransom for the captured officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Long'an submitted a further memorial: "Tenglong had entrusted gold to Wang Wanbang to reward officers and men from Bawang and Buladike who strayed from the route and returned safely. Yuanjun induced Wanbang to draft a document claiming that Guilin had paid ransom for captured troops.

sentences.zh: 事為元俊陷。

translations.literal: The affair was a frame-up by Yuanjun."
translations.idiomatic: The whole affair was a trap laid by Yuanjun."

sentences.zh: 」上乃怒，責元俊奸狡負恩，命奪職逮問，籍其家。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon grew angry, reproached Yuanjun for treacherous craftiness and ingratitude, ordered his rank stripped and him arrested for interrogation, and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flew into a rage, denounced Yuanjun as treacherous and ungrateful, stripped him of rank, ordered his arrest, and confiscated his estate.

sentences.zh: 參贊阿桂疏言：「元俊在川日久，熟番情，為近邊土司所信服。

translations.literal: Campaign Counselor Agui memorialized, saying: "Yuanjun has been long in Sichuan, is thoroughly familiar with tribal conditions, and is trusted by the frontier chieftains nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Counselor Agui memorialized: "Yuanjun has served in Sichuan for many years, knows frontier tribal affairs intimately, and enjoys the confidence of neighboring chieftains.

sentences.zh: 諸將能馭番無出其右。

translations.literal: Among the generals, none surpasses him in ability to command the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the commanders, none handles the tribes better than he does.

sentences.zh: 臣遇事多與詢商，冀收指臂之效。

translations.literal: Your servant consults with him on most affairs, hoping to gain the effect of an arm and finger working together.
translations.idiomatic: I consult him on nearly every matter in the hope of making our efforts work as one coordinated force.

sentences.zh: 乞恩仍留軍中，倘奮勉出力，使詐使貪，原所不廢；

translations.literal: I beg grace to keep him still in the army; if he exerts himself diligently, employing craft and greed is not in itself to be discarded;
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to let him remain with the army. If he throws himself into the fight, his cunning and appetite for gain may yet be turned to good use;

sentences.zh: 如剛愎逞私，即據實嚴劾。

translations.literal: if he is obstinate and indulges private aims, then I shall impeach him strictly according to fact."
translations.idiomatic: but if he grows obstinate and pursues private ends, I shall impeach him without mercy."

sentences.zh: 」上命留總兵，還所籍財產。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered him retained as brigade general and his confiscated property returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor allowed him to retain his rank as brigade general and ordered his confiscated property restored.

sentences.zh: 元俊同副都統永平、博靈阿等潛赴墨壟溝，進至郡崢。

translations.literal: Yuanjun together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Yongping, Boling'a, and others secretly proceeded to Molong Gorge and advanced to Junzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun, Vice Commander-in-Chief Yongping, Boling'a, and others made a stealthy advance to Molong Gorge and pushed on to Junzheng.

sentences.zh: 乘月督軍登山薄賊卡，正大霧，我師騰躍入卡，克山樑三道、碉卡二十有四，進克格魯克石。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the moonlight, he supervised the army in climbing the mountain to press close to the rebel passes; a great fog had just risen, and our troops leaped into the passes, capturing three mountain ridges and twenty-four tower-passes, and advancing to capture Geluke Stone.
translations.idiomatic: Under cover of moonlight he led his men up the slopes to assault the rebel passes. A thick fog had settled in, and the Qing troops vaulted into the passes, seizing three ridges and twenty-four tower-forts before advancing to take Geluke Stone.

sentences.zh: 金川酋圖佔丹壩官寨，綽斯甲布土司發兵往助，阿桂奏令元俊增兵往剿，未行，卒於軍。

translations.literal: The Jinchuan chieftain plotted to seize the Dandan official stockade; the Chosichab chieftain sent troops to assist. Agui memorialized ordering Yuanjun to add troops and proceed in suppression, but before he set out he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinchuan chief tried to seize the Dandan official fortress, the Chosichab chieftain sent reinforcements. Agui recommended that Yuanjun lead additional troops against them, but before he could march he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 元俊在邊久，善馭諸土司。

translations.literal: Yuanjun had been long on the frontier and was skilled in managing the various chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun had served on the frontier for many years and excelled at managing the native chieftains.

sentences.zh: 往時賚諸土司繒帛輒窳敝，元俊必以善者，諸土司皆喜。

translations.literal: In former times the silk bestowed on the chieftains was always shoddy and worn; Yuanjun always gave good quality, and all the chieftains were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts of silk to the chieftains had often been shoddy, but Yuanjun always presented fine cloth, to their great satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 元俊出行邊，諸土司率妻子出謁，畀以茶、菸、簪珥，視若家人。

translations.literal: When Yuanjun traveled the frontier, the chieftains would lead out their wives and children to pay respects; he would give them tea, tobacco, hairpins, and earrings, treating them like family.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yuanjun toured the frontier, chieftains brought out their wives and children to greet him. He gave them tea, tobacco, pins, and earrings and treated them like members of his own household.

sentences.zh: 稍不循法度，即訶譴，皆悚息聽命。

translations.literal: If they were slightly out of line with regulations, he would rebuke and reproach them, and all would tremble and obey his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if they stepped even slightly outside the rules, he scolded them sharply, and they trembled before obeying his orders.

sentences.zh: 打箭爐徼外夾壩出沒，元俊至，無敢犯行李者。

translations.literal: Outside the Dajianlu frontier, bandits called jiaba came and went; when Yuanjun arrived, none dared molest his baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits known as jiaba prowled beyond the Dajianlu frontier, but once Yuanjun appeared none dared touch his baggage.

sentences.zh: 諸番小有動靜，爭來告，以故元俊諸所措置皆中窾要。

translations.literal: Whenever the tribes had the slightest movement, they vied to come and report; for this reason all of Yuanjun's measures hit the vital point.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes rushed to report the slightest stir, which is why Yuanjun's every measure struck at the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 其得罪，上亦知其枉。

translations.literal: When he was punished, the emperor also knew he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he was punished, the emperor knew the charge was unjust.

sentences.zh: 既卒，其子猶戍邊。

translations.literal: After he died, his son was still garrisoned on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son remained on frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，金川平。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, Jinchuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 41 (1776), Jinchuan was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 元俊部將張芝元請於阿桂，謂元俊有功無罪，徒以忤專閫被羅織，語甚切。

translations.literal: Yuanjun's subordinate general Zhang Zhiyuan petitioned Agui, saying Yuanjun had merit and no crime, and had been framed only for offending the supreme commander; his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun's subordinate Zhang Zhiyuan appealed to Agui, arguing that Yuanjun was guilty of nothing and had been framed solely for defying the supreme commander; his plea was passionate and pointed.

sentences.zh: 阿桂為疏請，赦其子還。

translations.literal: Agui memorialized on his behalf, and the son was pardoned and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Agui submitted a memorial on his behalf, and the emperor pardoned Yuanjun's son and allowed him to return home.

sentences.zh: 薛琮，陝西咸寧人。

translations.literal: Xue Cong was a native of Xianning in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Cong came from Xianning in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父翼鳳，河南南陽鎮總兵。

translations.literal: His father Yifeng was brigade general of the Nanyang Garrison in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yifeng served as brigade general of the Nanyang garrison in Henan.

sentences.zh: 琮以廕生入巡捕營。

translations.literal: Cong entered the Patrol Battalion by hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Cong entered service in the Patrol Battalion through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 累遷四川漳臘營參將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to battalion major of the Zhangla Camp in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to battalion major of the Zhangla Camp in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 阿爾泰討金川，以琮從。

translations.literal: When Altai campaigned against Jinchuan, Cong accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Altai campaigned against Jinchuan, Cong served under his command.

sentences.zh: 克納頂、邊谷諸碉寨。

translations.literal: He captured Nadai, Biangu, and other towers and stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Nadai, Biangu, and other tower-forts.

sentences.zh: 溫福代阿爾泰視師，攻巴朗拉，琮戰最力。

translations.literal: Wenfu replaced Altai in supervising the army and attacked Balangla; Cong fought with the greatest exertion.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenfu replaced Altai as commander and assaulted Balangla, Cong fought with exceptional vigor.

sentences.zh: 又克卡丫，取通甲木。

translations.literal: He again captured Kaya and took Tong'anmu.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Kaya and secured the route to Jiamu.

sentences.zh: 攻阿仰東山，總督桂林與都統鐵保、提督汪騰龍將兵取墨壟溝，令琮將三千人自甲木、噶爾金後繞山道應大軍夾擊。

translations.literal: Attacking the Ayang Eastern Mountain, Governor Guilin together with Commander-in-Chief Tiebao and Provincial Military Commissioner Wang Tenglong led troops to take Molong Gorge, ordering Cong to command three thousand men from behind Jiamu and Ga'erjin by a mountain route to coordinate with the main army in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Ayang Eastern Mountain, Governor Guilin, Commander-in-Chief Tiebao, and Provincial Military Commissioner Wang Tenglong advanced on Molong Gorge while ordering Cong to lead three thousand men around the heights behind Jiamu and Ga'erjin to strike the enemy in concert with the main force.

sentences.zh: 桂林中道引還卡丫，又檄鐵保、騰龍令退。

translations.literal: Guilin turned back midway to Kaya, and again issued orders to Tiebao and Tenglong to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin turned back halfway to Kaya and ordered Tiebao and Tenglong to withdraw as well.

sentences.zh: 琮深入，糧盡，待桂林不至。

translations.literal: Cong had penetrated deep; provisions were exhausted, and he waited for Guilin, who did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Cong had pushed deep into enemy territory, exhausted his supplies, and waited in vain for Guilin.

sentences.zh: 桂林令都司廣著赴援。

translations.literal: Guilin ordered Brigade Commander Guangzhu to go to his relief.
translations.idiomatic: Guilin finally ordered Brigade Commander Guangzhu to march to his relief.

sentences.zh: 賊據高峰曰博六古通，險阻，廣著師不得度。

translations.literal: The rebels held a high peak called Bolugutong, rugged and perilous; Guangzhu's force could not cross it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the formidable height called Bolugutong, and Guangzhu's column could not get through.

sentences.zh: 琮督兵直進，毀柵十餘，奪碉七十餘。

translations.literal: Cong supervised the troops in a direct advance, destroying more than ten palisades and seizing more than seventy towers.
translations.idiomatic: Cong pressed straight ahead, destroying more than ten palisades and capturing more than seventy towers.

sentences.zh: 賊力拒，琮督兵仰攻，中槍，沒於陣，軍盡覆，同死者都司張清士、陳定國等二十五人。

translations.literal: The rebels resisted fiercely; Cong supervised the troops in an uphill assault, was struck by a musket ball, and perished in battle; the army was completely destroyed, and those who died with him included Brigade Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo and twenty-five others in all.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels resisted fiercely. Cong led an uphill assault, was struck by musket fire, and fell in battle. His entire force was wiped out, and twenty-five officers died with him, including Brigade Commanders Zhang Qingshi and Chen Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 阿桂破翁古爾壟，立祠戰地祀琮等。

translations.literal: When Agui captured Wenguerlong, he erected a shrine on the battlefield to sacrifice to Cong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: After Agui captured Wenguerlong, he erected a battlefield shrine to honor Cong and his fallen comrades.

sentences.zh: 琮在諸將中號能戰，元俊與最厚。

translations.literal: Among the generals Cong was known as able in battle; Yuanjun was closest to him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the commanders Cong was renowned for his fighting prowess, and Yuanjun was especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與期旦日會師，孰後至當斬。

translations.literal: They once agreed to join forces at dawn the next day, and whoever arrived late would be executed.
translations.idiomatic: They once agreed to rendezvous at dawn the next day on pain of death for whichever arrived late.

sentences.zh: 琮至後二刻，元俊遣騎持刀呼取薛參將頭。

translations.literal: Cong arrived two quarters of an hour late; Yuanjun sent a rider with a drawn blade calling for Battalion Major Xue's head.
translations.idiomatic: Cong arrived half an hour late, and Yuanjun sent a mounted messenger with drawn sword demanding the head of Battalion Major Xue.

sentences.zh: 琮望見笑曰：「琮頭當與賊，不與公也！

translations.literal: Cong saw him and laughed, saying: "Cong's head is for the rebels, not for you!
translations.idiomatic: Cong spotted him and laughed: "My head is for the enemy, not for you!

sentences.zh: 」奮前奪數碉反。

translations.literal: " He charged forward, seized several towers, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He charged forward, captured several towers, and returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 元俊猶為琮請罪，以功論贖乃已。

translations.literal: Yuanjun still pleaded guilt on Cong's behalf; only when merit was weighed against the offense was the matter dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun still interceded on Cong's behalf, and the affair was dropped only after his battlefield merit offset the offense.

sentences.zh: 及桂林誤琮戰沒，元俊憤激論劾，卒以是得罪。

translations.literal: When Guilin's error led to Cong's death in battle, Yuanjun in indignant fury memorialized in impeachment, and in the end was punished on that account.
translations.idiomatic: When Guilin's blunder cost Cong his life, Yuanjun impeached him in a fury and was himself punished in the end for doing so.

sentences.zh: 張芝元，四川清溪人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyuan was a native of Qingxi in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyuan came from Qingxi in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 以千總從副將軍明亮徵金川有功，積官至越巂營參將。

translations.literal: As company commander he followed Deputy General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign with merit, and through accumulated promotions reached battalion major of the Yuexi Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as company commander under Deputy General Mingliang in the Jinchuan campaign, he distinguished himself and rose through successive promotions to battalion major of the Yuexi Camp.

sentences.zh: 金川酋以番僧诇軍事，芝元言於明亮曰：「軍事每為賊知，非去其諜，滅賊無日矣。

translations.literal: The Jinchuan chieftain used Tibetan monks to spy on military affairs. Zhiyuan said to Mingliang: "Our military affairs are always known to the rebels; unless their spies are removed, there will be no day of destroying the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: The Jinchuan chief used Tibetan monks to spy on Qing operations. Zhiyuan told Mingliang: "The enemy always knows our movements. Unless we eliminate their spies, we will never defeat them."

sentences.zh: 」會大風雪，明亮命芝元率數十人偽若以他事出者，宿番僧寺中。

translations.literal: " At that time a great wind and snow arose; Mingliang ordered Zhiyuan to lead several dozen men pretending to go out on other business, and lodge in the Tibetan monks' temple.
translations.idiomatic: " A heavy blizzard followed. Mingliang ordered Zhiyuan to take several dozen men out under the pretense of routine business and lodge overnight in the monks' temple.

sentences.zh: 芝元故通番語，與僧飲甚歡，僧醉眠，芝元出寺聚柴焚之，僧皆死。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan was originally fluent in the tribal language; he drank merrily with the monks until they were drunk and asleep. Zhiyuan left the temple, gathered firewood, and burned it; all the monks died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan spoke the tribal languages fluently and drank freely with the monks until they passed out. He then left the temple, piled firewood against it, and set it ablaze, killing every monk inside.

sentences.zh: 賊諜斷，因招降其眾。

translations.literal: The rebels' intelligence network was cut off, and he was thereby able to induce their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With enemy intelligence broken, he was able to induce many rebels to surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋從成都將軍特成額駐兵江卡，捕夾壩，圍本肯賊寨，焚其碉，斃賊甚眾，擢懋功協副將。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he followed Chengdu General Techeng'e in garrisoning troops at Jiangka, capturing jiaba bandits, besieging the rebel stockade of Benken, burning its towers, and killing a great many rebels; he was promoted to deputy commander of the Maogong Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He later served under Chengdu General Techeng'e at Jiangka, hunted jiaba bandits, besieged the Benken rebel stockade, burned its towers, and killed large numbers of the enemy. He was promoted to deputy commander of the Maogong Battalion.

sentences.zh: 台灣林爽文為亂，芝元率屯練降番佐軍。

translations.literal: When Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Zhiyuan led garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Shuangwen rose in rebellion on Taiwan, Zhiyuan led garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen in support of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 參贊海蘭察等分攻大埔林、中林、大埔尾三莊，芝元為策應。

translations.literal: Campaign Counselor Hailancha and others divided forces to attack the three villages of Dapulin, Zhonglin, and Dapuwei; Zhiyuan served as supporting coordination.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Counselor Hailancha divided his forces to assault the villages of Dapulin, Zhonglin, and Dapuwei while Zhiyuan provided supporting coordination.

sentences.zh: 賊據小半天山，將軍福康安等自前山進，芝元與領隊大臣普爾普領兵別為一隊，夜半先發，繞大山夾攻賊後。

translations.literal: The rebels held Xiaobantian Mountain; General Fukang'an and others advanced from the front mountain; Zhiyuan together with Leading Minister Pu'erpu led troops in a separate column, setting out first at midnight and circling the great mountain to attack the rebels from the rear in concert.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Xiaobantian Mountain while General Fukang'an advanced from the front. Zhiyuan and Leading Minister Pu'erpu led a separate column that set out at midnight, swung around the main peak, and struck the enemy from the rear.

sentences.zh: 黎明，諸軍同抵山麓，攀援上，賊力拒，芝元先登，拔其柵，斬獲無算，並堵賊去路。

translations.literal: At dawn all armies reached the mountain foot together, climbed up by handholds; the rebels resisted fiercely; Zhiyuan was first to ascend, pulled up their palisades, killed and captured beyond counting, and also blocked the rebels' route of escape.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the columns met at the foot of the mountain and scaled the slopes together. The rebels resisted fiercely, but Zhiyuan was first to reach the top, tore down their palisades, killed or captured a great number of the enemy, and sealed off their line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爽文就擒。

translations.literal: Before long, Shuangwen was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lin Shuangwen was captured.

sentences.zh: 台灣平，擢建昌鎮總兵，圖形紫光閣，列前二十功臣。

translations.literal: When Taiwan was pacified, he was promoted to brigade general of Jianchang, his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the first twenty meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan was pacified he was promoted to brigade general of Jianchang, had his portrait enshrined in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and was numbered among the first twenty meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 尋調松潘鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to brigade general of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to brigade general of the Songpan garrison.

sentences.zh: 廓爾喀掠西藏濟嚨、聶拉木，上命芝元率屯練降番往討之。

translations.literal: Gurkhas raided Jilong and Nyalam in Tibet; the emperor ordered Zhiyuan to lead garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gurkha forces raided Jilong and Nyalam in Tibet, the emperor ordered Zhiyuan to lead garrison militia and surrendered tribesmen against them.

sentences.zh: 芝元至，值大雪，山谷皆滿。

translations.literal: When Zhiyuan arrived, heavy snow had fallen and the valleys were all filled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan arrived amid heavy snow that had filled every valley.

sentences.zh: 芝元手大刀指揮，士卒皆感激用命，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan personally wielded a great blade in command; the soldiers were all moved with gratitude and exerted themselves; the rebels were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wielding a great blade himself, Zhiyuan led from the front so inspiringly that his men fought with desperate loyalty and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 廓爾喀再叛，芝元偕提督成德督兵攻聶拉木，守拍甲嶺隘口斷賊援，聶拉木遂下；

translations.literal: When the Gurkhas rebelled again, Zhiyuan together with Provincial Military Commissioner Cheng De supervised troops in attacking Nyalam, held the pass at Paijialing to cut off rebel reinforcements, and Nyalam was then taken;
translations.idiomatic: When the Gurkhas rebelled again, Zhiyuan joined Provincial Military Commissioner Cheng De in assaulting Nyalam, held the Paijialing pass to sever enemy reinforcements, and Nyalam fell;

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻濟嚨，复克之，賊懼，乞降。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, they attacked Jilong and recovered it again; the rebels were afraid and begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the advantage, retook Jilong, and the enemy, terrified, sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，論平定廓爾喀功，再圖形紫光閣，列後十五功臣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, when the merit of pacifying the Gurkhas was assessed, his portrait was again placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was ranked among the later fifteen meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 58, when honors for pacifying the Gurkhas were awarded, his portrait was again placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor and he was numbered among the later fifteen meritorious officials.

sentences.zh: 芝元少以小校事元俊，後乃雪元俊枉。

translations.literal: In his youth Zhiyuan served Yuanjun as a junior officer; later he vindicated Yuanjun's wrongful punishment.
translations.idiomatic: As a young officer Zhiyuan had served under Yuanjun, and in later years he cleared Yuanjun's name of unjust charges.

sentences.zh: 人以是多芝元，亦益賢元俊能知人也。

translations.literal: People therefore praised Zhiyuan all the more, and also admired Yuanjun all the more for his ability to recognize men.
translations.idiomatic: People admired Zhiyuan all the more for this, and came to esteem Yuanjun still higher for his eye in choosing men.

sentences.zh: 董天弼，字霖蒼，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Dong Tianbi, whose style name was Lincang, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Tianbi, courtesy name Lincang, came from Daxing in the Shuntian metropolitan district.

sentences.zh: 自武進士授四川提標前營守備。

translations.literal: By military jinshi degree he was appointed garrison commandant of the Front Camp of the Sichuan Provincial Military Command.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military examinations, he was appointed garrison commandant of the Front Camp under the Sichuan provincial military command.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，師徵金川，天弼在軍有功。

translations.literal: In the early Qianlong reign, when the army campaigned against Jinchuan, Tianbi served in the army with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qianlong years, during the Jinchuan campaigns, Tianbi distinguished himself in the field.

sentences.zh: 累遷維​​州協副將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Weizhou Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to deputy commander of the Weizhou Battalion.

sentences.zh: 金川酋郎卡攻丹壩土司，天弼偕游擊宋元俊諭郎卡歸所掠，毀所築碉，兵罷，遷松潘鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Dandan chieftain, Tianbi together with Acting Colonel Song Yuanjun instructed Langka to return what he had seized and destroy the towers he had built; when the troops were dismissed he was transferred to brigade general of Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinchuan chieftain Langka attacked the Dandan chieftain, Tianbi and Acting Colonel Song Yuanjun compelled him to return his plunder and dismantle his fortifications. After the campaign ended Tianbi was transferred to brigade general of Songpan.

sentences.zh: 旋擢四川提督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Provincial Military Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Provincial Military Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 郭羅克部劫西藏入貢喇嘛，上命天弼按治，未得其渠，詔責其苟且。

translations.literal: The Golok tribe robbed the tribute-bearing lamas of Tibet; the emperor ordered Tianbi to investigate and punish them, but he did not capture their ringleader, and an edict reproached him for perfunctoriness.
translations.idiomatic: When Golok tribesmen robbed Tibetan tribute lamas, the emperor ordered Tianbi to punish them, but he failed to capture the ringleader and was rebuked by edict for half-hearted effort.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，小金川土司澤旺子僧格桑為亂，攻鄂克什土司色達克拉，圍其寨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, Senggesang, son of the Little Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, rebelled, attacked the Ekezhi chieftain Sedakela, and besieged his stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 35, Senggesang, son of the Little Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, rose in revolt, attacked Ekezhi Chieftain Sedakela, and besieged his fortress.

sentences.zh: 天弼督兵駐達木巴宗，檄僧格桑斂兵退色達克拉，以其寨糧盡，乞徙達木巴宗。

translations.literal: Tianbi supervised troops stationed at Damubazong and issued an order to Senggesang to withdraw his forces from Sedakela; because the stockade's provisions were exhausted, he begged to move to Damubazong.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi stationed troops at Damubazong and ordered Senggesang to withdraw from Sedakela's fortress. When Sedakela's supplies ran out, he begged to relocate to Damubazong.

sentences.zh: 天弼與總督阿爾泰議留兵戍焉。

translations.literal: Tianbi together with Governor Altai discussed leaving troops to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi and Governor Altai agreed to leave a garrison there.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，僧格桑复圍達木巴宗，並略木耳宗、巴朗拉諸地。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, Senggesang again besieged Damubazong and also seized Mu'erzong, Balangla, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36, Senggesang again besieged Damubazong and overran Mu'erzong, Balangla, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 天弼自打箭爐出邊，徵省標及松潘、維州諸鎮協兵，行至眠龍岡，賊已得巴朗拉，築碉卡為久守計，且斷我兵路。

translations.literal: Tianbi set out from the frontier at Dajianlu, mobilized the provincial standard troops and the forces of Songpan, Weizhou, and other garrisons, and when he reached Mianlonggang the rebels had already taken Balangla, built towers and passes for a long defense, and cut off our army's route.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi marched from Dajianlu, mustered provincial troops and garrison forces from Songpan and Weizhou, and reached Mianlonggang only to find the rebels already holding Balangla, fortifying tower-pass strongpoints for a prolonged defense, and severing his line of advance.

sentences.zh: 天弼議襲山神溝以解達木巴宗圍，尋將四百人自山神溝至德爾密，克碉七，賊竄走；

translations.literal: Tianbi planned to strike Shanshen Gorge to relieve the siege of Damubazong; soon he led four hundred men from Shanshen Gorge to De'ermi, captured seven towers, and the rebels fled;
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi planned a strike through Shanshen Gorge to relieve Damubazong. He led four hundred men along that route to De'ermi, captured seven towers, and drove the rebels off;

sentences.zh: 再進取畢旺拉，賊乘霧來犯，土兵驚潰，德爾密、畢旺拉皆陷。

translations.literal: advancing again to take Biwangla; the rebels took advantage of fog to attack, the native soldiers were startled and routed, and both De'ermi and Biwangla fell.
translations.idiomatic: then advanced on Biwangla. The rebels attacked through the fog, the native auxiliaries panicked and fled, and both De'ermi and Biwangla were lost.

sentences.zh: 天弼疏請罪，上以天弼所將兵本少，總督阿爾泰不預策應援，宥其罪，諭以「當奪勉。

translations.literal: Tianbi memorialized requesting punishment; the emperor, considering that the troops Tianbi commanded were originally few and that Governor Altai had not planned support in advance, pardoned his offense and instructed him: "You must strive with redoubled effort.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi submitted a confession. The emperor noted that Tianbi had commanded too few men and that Governor Altai had failed to plan reinforcements, pardoned him, and admonished: "You must fight all the harder.

sentences.zh: 再不努力，獲罪滋重矣」。

translations.literal: If you do not exert yourself again, your guilt will grow all the heavier."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail again, your punishment will be far worse."

sentences.zh: 天弼復將五百人自木坪陟堯磧，順山攻甲金達對面山梁，取碉二。

translations.literal: Tianbi again led five hundred men from Muping up the Yaoqi heights, following the mountain to attack the ridge opposite Jiajinda, and captured two towers.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi led five hundred men from Muping up the Yaoqi slopes and along the ridge opposite Jiajinda, capturing two towers.

sentences.zh: 天弼以鄂克什牛廠當要道，分兵殲守廠賊，駐軍其地；

translations.literal: Tianbi, considering the Ekezhi cattle pasture on a vital route, divided his forces to annihilate the rebels guarding the pasture and stationed troops there;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Ekezhi cattle pasture lay on a vital route, Tianbi detached troops to destroy the rebels holding it and garrisoned the position;

sentences.zh: 乘勝上下截擊，木坪、鄂克什諸土司錯壤，要隘皆為我軍有。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory with attacks from above and below, and with the chieftains of Muping, Ekezhi, and others on adjoining territories, all strategic passes came into our army's possession.
translations.idiomatic: He followed up with converging strikes from above and below until, with the interlocking domains of the Muping, Ekezhi, and neighboring chieftains, every strategic pass fell under Qing control.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊复襲據牛廠。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels again attacked and seized the cattle pasture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels retook the cattle pasture.

sentences.zh: 上以阿爾泰師久無功，奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Altai's army had long been without success, stripped him of his rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Altai of rank because his army had achieved nothing after months of campaigning.

sentences.zh: 因責：「天弼始終貽誤，與阿爾泰同罪，奪官，留軍中充伍。

translations.literal: and reproached: "Tianbi from beginning to end has caused delay and error, sharing Altai's guilt; strip his rank and keep him in the army as a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him: "Tianbi has bungled from start to finish and shares Altai's guilt. Strip his rank and keep him in the ranks as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 如更退縮，正軍法。

translations.literal: If he retreats again, apply military law."
translations.idiomatic: If he retreats again, execute him under military law."

sentences.zh: 」尋命下成都獄。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he was ordered imprisoned in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon ordered imprisoned in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 詔未至，天弼以甲金達山峻不可上，求間道，得溝在兩崖間。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Tianbi, finding the Jiajinda mountain too steep to ascend, sought a bypath and found a gorge between two cliffs.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Tianbi found Jiajinda Mountain too steep to assault directly, searched for a detour, and discovered a gorge between two cliffs.

sentences.zh: 會大風雪，天弼率兵自溝中潛度，遂至達木巴宗，擊僧格桑色達克拉；

translations.literal: A great wind and snow arose; Tianbi led troops in a secret crossing through the gorge, reached Damubazong, and attacked Senggesang and Sedakela;
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard struck. Tianbi led his men in a stealthy crossing through the gorge, reached Damubazong, and struck Senggesang and Sedakela;

sentences.zh: 潰圍出，並克木耳宗，迎溫福師與會。

translations.literal: broke the siege and came out, also captured Mu'erzong, and joined Wenfu's army in meeting.
translations.idiomatic: broke the encirclement, also retook Mu'erzong, and linked up with Wenfu's main force.

sentences.zh: 上聞，命貸死，留軍中。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he ordered his death sentence commuted and that he be kept in the army.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the emperor commuted the death sentence and kept him with the army.

sentences.zh: 阿桂令天弼監火藥軍械。

translations.literal: Agui ordered Tianbi to supervise gunpowder and military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Agui put Tianbi in charge of gunpowder and ordnance.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，師克資哩，阿桂令天弼將五百人駐焉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, when the army captured Zili, Agui ordered Tianbi to lead five hundred men to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 37, after Zili was captured, Agui assigned Tianbi five hundred men to garrison the post.

sentences.zh: 尋予副將銜，授重慶鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was given the brevet rank of deputy general and appointed brigade general of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received brevet rank as deputy general and was appointed brigade general of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 命督兵赴曾頭溝，進至梭磨，梭磨土婦請以千人從。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise troops proceeding to Zengtou Gorge and advancing to Suomo; the Suomo tribal woman requested to follow with one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to lead troops to Zengtou Gorge and on to Suomo, where the Suomo chieftain's wife offered a thousand warriors to join him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When this was reported, he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported to the throne, he was awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 天弼督兵攻堪卓溝，自間道出納云達，深入賊境五十餘裡，克山樑三，破碉卡三十餘、木城三。

translations.literal: Tianbi supervised troops in attacking Kanzhuo Gorge, came out by a bypath to Nayunda, penetrated more than fifty li into rebel territory, captured three mountain ridges, and broke more than thirty towers and passes and three wooden forts.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi assaulted Kanzhuo Gorge, took a detour to Nayunda, and pushed more than fifty li into enemy territory, seizing three ridges and destroying more than thirty tower-forts and three wooden strongholds.

sentences.zh: 迎溫福師會於布朗郭宗，克大板昭、木丫寨，得碉三十六、卡十六。

translations.literal: He joined Wenfu's army in meeting at Bulangguozong, captured Dabanzhao and Muyazhai, and took thirty-six towers and sixteen passes.
translations.idiomatic: He rendezvoused with Wenfu at Bulangguozong, captured Dabanzhao and Muyazhai, and took thirty-six towers and sixteen passes.

sentences.zh: 上以溫福已得布朗郭宗進克底木達，天弼所克不過空寨，疏語頗鋪張，手敕戒之。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Wenfu had already taken Bulangguozong and advanced to capture Dimuda while what Tianbi had taken were only empty stockades, and that the memorial's language was rather exaggerated, personally wrote an edict admonishing him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that Wenfu had already taken Bulangguozong and advanced on Dimuda while Tianbi's gains were mostly empty stockades, found his memorial exaggerated, and sent a personal edict of warning.

sentences.zh: 尋授領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Leading Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Leading Minister.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，復為四川提督。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was again made Provincial Military Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38 he was restored as Provincial Military Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時小金川已定，溫福督師進討大金川，令天弼以五百人守底木達。

translations.literal: At that time Little Jinchuan had been pacified; Wenfu supervised the army in advancing to attack Great Jinchuan and ordered Tianbi to guard Dimuda with five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Little Jinchuan had been pacified, and Wenfu led the advance against Great Jinchuan with Tianbi assigned five hundred men to hold Dimuda.

sentences.zh: 溫福進駐木果木，號大營；

translations.literal: Wenfu advanced and encamped at Muguo Wood, called the Great Camp;
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu advanced to Muguo Wood and established the main camp there;

sentences.zh: 底木達當賊來路，為要隘。

translations.literal: Dimuda lay on the rebels' route of advance and was a strategic pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dimuda stood on the enemy's line of advance and was a critical pass.

sentences.zh: 溫福檄三百人益大營，又去其後援。

translations.literal: Wenfu ordered three hundred men transferred to reinforce the Great Camp, thereby removing his rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu requisitioned three hundred of his men for the main camp, stripping away his rear support.

sentences.zh: 時溫福以軍屢勝，不以賊為意。

translations.literal: At that time Wenfu, because the army had repeatedly won victories, did not take the rebels seriously.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu, emboldened by repeated victories, took the enemy lightly.

sentences.zh: 金川頭人七圖葛拉爾思甲布等以千餘人詐降，溫福使與廝養雜處，因誘諸降人為變，諗底木達兵弱無後援，六月乙丑朔，潛自山後擁眾攻底木達，天弼率所部二百人抽刀力戰，至夜半，賊以鳥槍數百環擊，殺之。

translations.literal: The Jinchuan headmen Qitugela'er Sijabu and others feigned surrender with more than a thousand men; Wenfu had them mixed with servants and attendants, then induced the surrendered men to mutiny, reckoning that Dimuda's troops were few and without rear support. On the first day of the sixth month, yichou, they secretly came from behind the mountain with a crowd to attack Dimuda. Tianbi led his two hundred men, drawing blades to fight fiercely; by midnight the rebels surrounded them with several hundred muskets and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchuan headmen including Qitugela'er Sijabu feigned surrender with more than a thousand followers. Wenfu quartered them among camp servants, then incited the supposed defectors to revolt, calculating that Dimuda was weakly held and unsupported. On the first day of the sixth month they struck from the rear with a mass assault. Tianbi led his remaining two hundred men in a desperate sword fight, but by midnight hundreds of enemy muskets had ringed his position and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 越九日，劫大營，溫福亦死焉。

translations.literal: Nine days later they raided the Great Camp, and Wenfu also died there.
translations.idiomatic: Nine days later they overran the main camp, and Wenfu was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 上先命天弼駐丹壩，旋命移駐布朗郭宗，軍中傳賊來犯。

translations.literal: The emperor had first ordered Tianbi to garrison Dandan, then ordered him transferred to Bulangguozong; in the army it was rumored that rebels were coming to attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had first ordered Tianbi to hold Dandan, then to move to Bulangguozong, while camp rumor spread that the enemy was about to strike.

sentences.zh: 時天弼方屯美諾，上命奪官逮治。

translations.literal: At that time Tianbi was encamped at Meinuo; the emperor ordered his rank stripped and him arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi was then encamped at Meinuo, and the emperor ordered him stripped of rank and arrested.

sentences.zh: 總督劉秉恬疏言：「天弼自美諾馳赴底木達，途遇賊，右脅中槍死。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Bingtian memorialized, saying: "Tianbi galloped from Meinuo toward Dimuda, met rebels on the way, was struck by a musket ball in the right side, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Bingtian reported: "Tianbi had galloped from Meinuo toward Dimuda, encountered rebels on the road, was shot in the right side, and died.

sentences.zh: 」仍以貽誤軍事籍其家，戍其子舉人聯伊犁。

translations.literal: " Nevertheless, for having caused delay and harm to military affairs, his household property was confiscated, and his son Lian, a provincial graduate, was banished to garrison duty in Yili.
translations.idiomatic: " Nevertheless, for dereliction in the campaign his estate was confiscated and his son Lian, a provincial graduate, was banished to garrison duty in Yili.

sentences.zh: 金川既平，獲七圖葛拉爾思甲布，傳送熱河行在，廷訊，具言天弼死事時力戰狀，乃赦聯還，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitugela'er Sijabu was captured and sent to the imperial residence at Rehe; at a court interrogation he fully described how fiercely Tianbi had fought at the time of his death in battle, and Lian was thereupon pardoned and allowed to return, appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinchuan was pacified, Qitugela'er Sijabu was captured and brought to the emperor at Rehe. At his interrogation he described how fiercely Tianbi had fought before he fell, and Lian was pardoned, allowed to return, and appointed Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 柴大紀，浙江江山人。

translations.literal: Chai Daji was a native of Jiangshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Daji came from Jiangshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 自武進士授福建守備。

translations.literal: By military jinshi degree he was appointed garrison commandant in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the military examinations, he was appointed garrison commandant in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 累擢至海壇鎮總兵，移台灣鎮。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to brigade general of Haitan and then transferred to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to brigade general of Haitan and was then transferred to command the Taiwan garrison.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十一年十一月，林爽文亂起。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifty-first year of Qianlong, Lin Shuangwen's rebellion broke out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Qianlong 51, Lin Shuangwen's rebellion erupted.

sentences.zh: 爽文漳州人，徙彰化，所居村曰大里杙。

translations.literal: Shuangwen was a man of Zhangzhou who had moved to Zhanghua; the village where he lived was called Dalijiao.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen was a native of Zhangzhou who had settled in Zhanghua at the village of Dalijiao.

sentences.zh: 時奸民相聚，號天地會，漳州人莊煙為之魁，爽文與相結，謀為變。

translations.literal: At that time wicked commoners gathered together, calling themselves the Heaven and Earth Society; Zhuang Yan of Zhangzhou was their leader, and Shuangwen joined with them to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked elements had formed the Heaven and Earth Society under the Zhangzhou native Zhuang Yan as leader, and Shuangwen joined them in plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 台灣知府孫景燧馳詣彰化，督知縣俞峻、副將赫生額、游擊耿世文捕治，焚數小村以怵之。

translations.literal: Taiwan Prefect Sun Jingsui hurried to Zhanghua, supervised District Magistrate Yu Jun, Deputy General Hesheng'e, and Acting Colonel Geng Shiwen in arresting and punishing them, and burned several small villages to intimidate them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan Prefect Sun Jingsui rushed to Zhanghua and directed District Magistrate Yu Jun, Deputy General Hesheng'e, and Acting Colonel Geng Shiwen to arrest the conspirators, burning several villages to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 爽文因民怨，夜糾其徒來襲，赫生額等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Shuangwen, relying on popular resentment, gathered his followers by night to attack; Hesheng'e and the others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting popular resentment, Shuangwen rallied his followers in a night attack that killed Hesheng'e and his officers.

sentences.zh: 明日，遂破彰化，景燧亦殉焉。

translations.literal: The next day they broke Zhanghua, and Jingsui also died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they stormed Zhanghua, and Jingsui died defending the city.

sentences.zh: 傍攻諸羅、鳳山，皆陷。

translations.literal: They attacked Zhuluo and Fengshan on the flanks, and both fell.
translations.idiomatic: They then overran Zhuluo and Fengshan as well.

sentences.zh: 大紀時以總兵守府城，賊分道來攻，大紀出駐鹽埕橋御之，擊沉賊舟數十，馘千餘。

translations.literal: Daji was then brigade general defending the prefectural city; the rebels came to attack by separate routes; Daji went out to garrison Yancheng Bridge to resist them, sank several dozen rebel boats, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Daji, then brigade general, held the prefectural capital. When rebels attacked along several routes he took position at Yancheng Bridge, sank dozens of their boats, and killed more than a thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 五十二年春，水師提督黃仕簡、陸路提督任承恩先後赴援。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifty-second year, Naval Commissioner Huang Shijian and Army Commissioner Ren Chengen successively came to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Qianlong 52, Naval Commissioner Huang Shijian and Army Commissioner Ren Chengen arrived in succession to reinforce the island.

sentences.zh: 大紀出攻諸羅，克之，即移軍守諸羅。

translations.literal: Daji went out to attack Zhuluo, captured it, and immediately moved his army to defend Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: Daji marched out, recaptured Zhuluo, and transferred his force there to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 旋以守府城功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, for his merit in defending the prefectural city, he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon awarded the peacock feather for defending the prefectural capital.

sentences.zh: 上以仕簡、承恩師久無功，授總督常青將軍，渡台灣視師。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shijian's and Chengen's armies had long been without success, appointed Governor Changqing as general and ordered him to cross to Taiwan to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huang Shijian and Ren Chengen had achieved nothing after months in the field, the emperor appointed Governor Changqing as commanding general and sent him to Taiwan to take charge.

sentences.zh: 爽文攻諸羅，自二月至四月凡十至，大紀督游擊楊起麟、守備邱能成等出戰，殺賊數千。

translations.literal: Shuangwen attacked Zhuluo; from the second month to the fourth month he came ten times in all. Daji supervised Acting Colonel Yang Qilin, Garrison Commandant Qiu Nengcheng, and others in going out to battle, killing several thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen assaulted Zhuluo ten times between the second and fourth months. Daji led Acting Colonel Yang Qilin, Garrison Commandant Qiu Nengcheng, and others in sorties that killed several thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 爽文之徒張慎徽偽降，大紀察其詐，置諸法。

translations.literal: Shuangwen's follower Zhang Shenhui feigned surrender; Daji detected the deception and executed him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangwen's follower Zhang Shenhui feigned surrender, but Daji saw through the ruse and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 台灣諸府縣皆編竹為城，不耐攻，大紀以忠義率兵民誓堅守。

translations.literal: The prefectures and districts of Taiwan all had walls woven of bamboo, which could not withstand attack; Daji led soldiers and civilians by loyalty and righteousness, swearing to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan's prefectures and districts were walled with woven bamboo that could not withstand assault, yet Daji rallied soldiers and civilians by appeal to loyalty and righteousness and swore to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 上嘉大紀勞，賜荷包、奶餅，下部議敘。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Daji's labors, bestowed a purse and milk cakes, and ordered the ministries to deliberate on rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Daji's exertions, sent him a purse and milk cakes as gifts, and ordered the ministries to consider his reward.

sentences.zh: 六月，授福建陸路提督，仍兼領台灣總兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Army Commissioner of Fujian while still concurrently commanding the Taiwan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was made Army Commissioner of Fujian while retaining command of the Taiwan garrison.

sentences.zh: 鹽水港者，諸羅通府城糧道也，賊來攻，大紀力御之。

translations.literal: Yanshui Harbor was the grain route from Zhuluo to the prefectural city; when rebels came to attack, Daji resisted them with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshui Harbor was Zhuluo's lifeline to the prefectural capital. When rebels attacked it, Daji defended it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 上促常青赴援，予大紀壯健巴圖魯名號，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: The emperor urged Changqing to hurry to reinforce; Daji was given the title of Valiant Baturu and made Campaign Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed Changqing to hurry to the relief while granting Daji the title Valiant Baturu and appointing him campaign counselor.

sentences.zh: 八月，上以常青衰老不能辦賊，命福康安為將軍，仍令大紀參贊；

translations.literal: In the eighth month the emperor, considering Changqing aged and unable to deal with the rebels, appointed Fukang'an as general while still keeping Daji as counselor;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, judging Changqing too old to defeat the rebels, the emperor appointed Fukang'an as commanding general while retaining Daji as counselor;

sentences.zh: 而常青令總兵魏大斌援諸羅，賊邀諸途，退駐鹿仔草；

translations.literal: but Changqing ordered Brigade General Wei Dabin to reinforce Zhuluo; the rebels intercepted him on every road, and he withdrew to garrison Luzicao;
translations.idiomatic: but Changqing ordered Brigade General Wei Dabin to relieve Zhuluo. Rebels blocked every route, and Wei withdrew to Luzicao;

sentences.zh: 復令總兵蔡攀龍援諸羅，大紀出戰，迎入城共守。

translations.literal: he again ordered Brigade General Cai Panlong to reinforce Zhuluo; Daji went out to battle and welcomed him into the city to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: then ordered Brigade General Cai Panlong to relieve Zhuluo. Daji fought his way out to meet him and brought him into the city for a joint defense.

sentences.zh: 上移大紀水師提督，而以陸路提督授攀龍。

translations.literal: The emperor transferred Daji to Naval Commissioner and gave the Army Commissionership to Panlong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promoted Daji to Naval Commissioner and gave Cai Panlong the army commissionership.

sentences.zh: 十一月，加大紀太子少保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Daji was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Daji was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 上以諸羅被圍久，縣民困守，奮力向義，更縣名為嘉義。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Zhuluo had long been besieged and the county people had struggled in defense while striving toward righteousness, changed the county name to Jiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhuluo's people had endured a long siege while holding firm in loyalty, the emperor renamed the county Jiayi, "Upholding Righteousness."

sentences.zh: 賊攻城益急，上密諭大紀：「不必堅執與城存亡，如遇事急，可率兵力戰，出城再圖進取。

translations.literal: The rebels pressed the siege ever more fiercely; the emperor secretly instructed Daji: "You need not insist on perishing with the city; if matters grow urgent, you may lead the troops in fierce battle, leave the city, and plan advance again later.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege intensified, the emperor secretly told Daji: "You need not die with the city. If matters grow desperate, break out with your troops and seek another opening for advance.

sentences.zh: 」大紀疏言：「諸羅居台灣南北之中，縣城四周積土植竹，環以深壕，壕上為短垣，置砲，防衛堅固。

translations.literal: " Daji memorialized, saying: "Zhuluo lies in the middle between north and south Taiwan; around the county seat earth is piled and bamboo planted, encircled by a deep moat, with a low wall above the moat and cannon emplaced; the defenses are solid.
translations.idiomatic: " Daji replied in a memorial: "Zhuluo stands at the center of the island. Its walls are built of earth and bamboo, ringed by a deep moat topped with a low parapet and cannon. The defenses are formidable.

sentences.zh: 一旦棄之而去，為賊所得，慮賊勢益張，鹽水港運道亦不能守。

translations.literal: If it is abandoned at once and falls to the rebels, I fear the rebel power will grow all the more, and the transport route at Yanshui Harbor also cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon it now, the rebels will grow stronger and we will lose Yanshui Harbor and our supply line as well.

sentences.zh: 且城廂內外居民及各莊避難入城者共四萬餘人，助餉協守，以至於今。

translations.literal: Moreover, residents inside and outside the city wards and refugees from the various villages who entered the city number more than forty thousand in all; they have helped with provisions and joined in defense down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: More than forty thousand people inside the walls and refugees from surrounding villages have shared provisions and joined the defense until now.

sentences.zh: 不忍將此數万生靈付逆賊毒手！

translations.literal: I cannot bear to deliver these tens of thousands of living souls into the rebels' cruel hands!
translations.idiomatic: I cannot abandon these tens of thousands of lives to rebel butchery!

sentences.zh: 惟有竭力保守，以待援兵。

translations.literal: I can only exert every effort to hold and preserve it, awaiting relief troops."
translations.idiomatic: I can only hold on with all my strength until relief arrives."

sentences.zh: 」上手詔謂：「所奏忠肝義，披覽為之墮淚！

translations.literal: " The emperor personally wrote an edict, saying: "What you have memorialized shows loyal heart and righteous courage; reading it, tears fell from my eyes!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wrote back in his own hand: "Your memorial shows a loyal and righteous heart. Reading it brought tears to my eyes!

sentences.zh: 大紀被圍日久，心志益堅，勉勵兵民，忍飢固守，惟知以國事民生為重。

translations.literal: Daji has long been besieged, yet his resolve grows ever firmer; he encourages soldiers and civilians, endures hunger in steadfast defense, and knows only to place state affairs and the people's lives first.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged for so long, Daji has only grown more resolute. He rallies soldiers and civilians, endures hunger, and holds the line with nothing but the welfare of the state and the people in mind.

sentences.zh: 古之名將，何以加之？

translations.literal: How could the famous generals of antiquity surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: What famous general of antiquity could do more?

sentences.zh: 」因封為一等義勇伯，世襲罔替，並命浙江巡撫琅玕予其家白金萬，促福康安赴援。

translations.literal: " He was therefore enfeoffed as a first-rank Baron of Righteous Courage with perpetual hereditary succession, and Zhejiang Governor Langgan was ordered to give his family ten thousand taels of white silver and to urge Fukang'an to hurry to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ennobled as a first-rank Baron of Righteous Courage with perpetual hereditary succession, Zhejiang Governor Langgan was ordered to grant his family ten thousand taels of silver, and Fukang'an was pressed to hurry to the relief.

sentences.zh: 十二月，福康安師至，嘉義圍解，大紀出迎，自以功高拜爵賞，又在圍城中，倥傯不具櫜鞬禮，福康安銜之，遂劾大紀詭詐，深染綠營習氣，不可倚任。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Fukang'an's army arrived and the siege of Jiayi was lifted. Daji went out to welcome him, considering himself high in merit for ennoblement and reward, and moreover having been in the besieged city, he was too harried to present full ceremonial arms and armor. Fukang'an resented this and thereupon impeached Daji for deceitful craftiness, deeply infected with Green Standard Army habits, and unfit to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fukang'an arrived and lifted the siege of Jiayi. Daji went out to greet him, confident that his ennoblement and rewards made him the hero of the hour, yet still harried from the siege and unable to observe full military courtesy. Fukang'an took offense and impeached him for deceit, deep Green Standard corruption, and unreliability.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「大紀駐守嘉義，賊百計攻圍，督率兵民，力為捍衛。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed, saying: "Daji garrisoned Jiayi; the rebels attacked and besieged by every stratagem; he supervised and led soldiers and civilians and strove to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Daji held Jiayi while the rebels assaulted it by every means. He led soldiers and civilians in a determined defense.

sentences.zh: 朕諭以力不能支，不妨全師而出。

translations.literal: I instructed him that if his strength could not hold, he might withdraw the whole force intact.
translations.idiomatic: I told him that if he could not hold, he might withdraw with his force intact.

sentences.zh: 大紀堅持定見，竭力固守，不忍以數萬生靈委之於賊。

translations.literal: Daji held firm to his settled view, exerted every effort to hold fast, and could not bear to deliver tens of thousands of living souls into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Daji held firm, fought on with all his strength, and refused to abandon tens of thousands of lives to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 朕閱其疏，為之墮淚。

translations.literal: When I read his memorial, tears fell for it.
translations.idiomatic: Reading his memorial moved me to tears.

sentences.zh: 福康安乃不能以朕之心為心乎？

translations.literal: Can Fukang'an not make my heart his own heart?
translations.idiomatic: Can Fukang'an not share my own view of the matter?

sentences.zh: 大紀嘗奏賊以車載槍砲攻城，今福康安言得賊攻城大車，又委棄槍砲，為我軍所得，足見大紀前奏不虛。

translations.literal: Daji once memorialized that the rebels used carts to carry muskets and cannon in attacking the city; now Fukang'an reports capturing the rebels' great siege carts and also abandoned muskets and cannon taken by our army, which fully shows Daji's earlier memorial was not false.
translations.idiomatic: Daji had reported that the rebels used siege carts mounted with muskets and cannon. Fukang'an now reports capturing those very carts along with abandoned firearms, proving Daji's earlier account true.

sentences.zh: 大紀又奏縣城食盡，地瓜、花生俱罄，以油K5充食。

translations.literal: Daji also memorialized that provisions in the county seat were exhausted, sweet potatoes and peanuts were all gone, and oil-pressing residue was used for food.
translations.idiomatic: Daji also reported that the city had run out of food, with sweet potatoes and peanuts exhausted and even oil-pressing residue eaten for sustenance.

sentences.zh: 當時義民助餉，未必遽至於此。

translations.literal: At that time loyal civilians helped with provisions, and matters may not have reached that point so quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal civilians were still contributing provisions then, and conditions may not yet have been quite so desperate.

sentences.zh: 但大紀望援心急，以食油K5為詞。

translations.literal: But Daji, anxious for relief, used eating oil residue as his plea.
translations.idiomatic: But Daji, desperate for relief, exaggerated by speaking of eating oil residue.

sentences.zh: 普吉保、恆瑞兩軍尚復觀望不進，若云猶有餘粟，則兩路赴援更緩。

translations.literal: The armies of Pujibao and Hengrui were still watching and not advancing; if it were said that grain still remained, then the two columns coming to reinforce would be even slower.
translations.idiomatic: The columns of Pujibao and Hengrui were still holding back. If it were reported that grain remained, those two relief forces would move even more slowly.

sentences.zh: 此時縣城存亡未可知，安怪大紀過甚其詞耶？

translations.literal: At that time whether the county seat would survive was still unknown; how can one blame Daji for overstating his words?
translations.idiomatic: With the city's fate still uncertain, how can one blame Daji for pressing his case so urgently?

sentences.zh: 大紀屢荷褒嘉，在福康安前禮節或有不謹，致為所憎，直揭其短。

translations.literal: Daji had repeatedly received praise and reward; before Fukang'an his etiquette may have been somewhat lacking, causing resentment, and Fukang'an directly exposed his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Daji had been repeatedly honored by the throne, but his manners toward Fukang'an may have been lacking, provoking resentment and a direct airing of his faults.

sentences.zh: 福康安當體朕心，略短取長，方得公忠體國之道。

translations.literal: Fukang'an ought to enter into my heart, overlook faults and take strengths, and only then attain the way of impartial loyalty in serving the state."
translations.idiomatic: Fukang'an should share my view, overlook faults in favor of merit, and thus practice true loyalty to the state."

sentences.zh: 」侍郎德成自浙江奉使還，受福康安指，訐大紀。

translations.literal: " Vice Minister Decheng returned from a mission in Zhejiang, received Fukang'an's direction, and denounced Daji.
translations.idiomatic: " Vice Minister Decheng, returning from a mission in Zhejiang at Fukang'an's instigation, denounced Daji.

sentences.zh: 上命福康安、李侍堯、徐嗣曾、琅玕按治，福康安臨致書軍機大臣，言：「大紀縱兵激民為變，其守嘉義，皆義民之力。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Fukang'an, Li Shiyao, Xu Siceng, and Langgan to investigate and settle the case. Fukang'an, on the eve of departure, wrote to the Grand Council ministers, saying: "Daji let his troops run wild and incited the people to revolt; his defense of Jiayi was entirely the work of loyal civilians.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Fukang'an, Li Shiyao, Xu Siceng, and Langgan to investigate. On the eve of the inquiry Fukang'an wrote the Grand Council: "Daji's troops provoked the people to revolt, and his defense of Jiayi owed everything to loyal civilians.

sentences.zh: 大紀聞命，欲引兵以退，義民不令出城，乃罷。

translations.literal: When Daji heard the order, he wished to lead his troops in withdrawal, but the loyal civilians would not let him leave the city, and the plan was abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: When Daji heard the order he tried to withdraw his troops, but the loyal civilians would not let him leave the city, and the attempt was abandoned."

sentences.zh: 」事聞，上諭謂：「守諸羅一事，朕不忍以為大紀罪，至其他聲名狼藉、縱兵激變諸狀，自當按治。

translations.literal: " When this was reported, the emperor instructed, saying: "In the matter of defending Zhuluo, I cannot bear to treat it as Daji's crime; as for his other disreputable conduct and letting troops incite rebellion, those should naturally be investigated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: " When this was reported, the emperor said: "I will not treat the defense of Zhuluo as Daji's crime, but his other misconduct and provoking revolt must be investigated.

sentences.zh: 」命奪大紀職，逮問。
