translations.literal: " He ordered Daji stripped of rank and arrested for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Daji stripped of rank and arrested.

sentences.zh: 福康安尋以大紀縱弛貪黷、貽誤軍機，議斬，送京師。

translations.literal: Fukang'an soon, on the grounds that Daji was lax, greedy, and corrupt and had harmed military affairs, recommended execution and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fukang'an soon recommended execution on charges of lax discipline, corruption, and dereliction, and sent Daji to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上命軍機大臣覆讞，大紀訴冤苦，並言德成有意週內，迫嘉義民證其罪，下廷訊，大紀猶力辯。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Grand Council ministers to review the verdict. Daji pleaded his bitter wrong, also saying Decheng had deliberately maneuvered on his behalf and compelled Jiayi civilians to testify to his guilt. The case was sent for court interrogation, and Daji still argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Grand Council to review the case. Daji protested his innocence, alleging that Decheng had rigged the proceedings and coerced Jiayi civilians into testifying against him. At the court interrogation Daji still argued vigorously.

sentences.zh: 五十三年七月辛巳，命如福康安議棄市，其子發伊犁為奴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifty-third year, on the day xinsi, he was ordered executed in public market according to Fukang'an's recommendation, and his son was banished to Yili as a slave.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day of the seventh month of Qianlong 53, he was ordered executed in public as Fukang'an had recommended, and his son was banished to Yili as a bondsman.

sentences.zh: 論曰：元俊、天弼在邊久，熟情偽，習形勢，諸番仰其威惠。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Yuanjun and Tianbi had been long on the frontier, were thoroughly familiar with truth and falsehood, were versed in terrain and situation, and the tribes looked up to their authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Yuanjun and Tianbi had served long on the frontier, knew tribal affairs inside out, understood the terrain, and the tribes respected both their authority and their goodwill.

sentences.zh: 元俊戹於桂林，激而欲自白，不得直；

translations.literal: Yuanjun suffered adversity at the hands of Guilin, was provoked and wished to clear himself, but could not obtain justice;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjun clashed with Guilin, was provoked into trying to clear his name, yet could not obtain justice;

sentences.zh: 微阿桂右之，罪且不測。

translations.literal: had it not been for Agui's support of him, his guilt would have been beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: had Agui not intervened on his behalf, his punishment might have been far worse.

sentences.zh: 天弼又見嫉於溫福，驅至寡之兵以投方張之寇，既死猶尚以為罪。

translations.literal: Tianbi was again envied and resented by Wenfu, driven with scant troops to throw himself against rebels in full expansion; even after death he was still treated as guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbi likewise earned Wenfu's jealousy, was sent with too few men against a rising enemy, and was still treated as guilty even after he died fighting.

sentences.zh: 若大紀有功無罪，為福康安所不容。

translations.literal: As for Daji, though he had merit and no crime, he could not be tolerated by Fukang'an.
translations.idiomatic: As for Daji, meritorious and innocent though he was, Fukang'an would not tolerate him.

sentences.zh: 高宗手詔，可謂曲折而詳盡矣，乃終不能貸其死。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong's personal edict may be called intricate and exhaustive, yet in the end he could not spare Daji from death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong's own edict in Daji's defense was subtle and thorough, yet even that could not save him from execution.

sentences.zh: 軍旅之際，捐肝腦，冒鋒刃，求尺寸之效，困於媢嫉，功不成而死於敵，若功成矣，而又死於法。

translations.literal: In the midst of military campaigns, men give liver and brains, brave blades edge, and seek the slightest effect; hampered by jealous rivalry, they die at the enemy's hands without achieving merit, or if merit is achieved, they yet die under the law.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign men give their lives and face the blade for the smallest gain. Jealousy thwarts them: some die by the enemy without winning glory; others win glory only to die by the law.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，可哀也已！

translations.literal: Alas, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how lamentable it is!
